warnings.text: You’re spending about £483 a month more than you take home.
From 2027 (age 32) your savings and investments can’t cover your spending. The gap is shown as an unfunded shortfall.
The projection doesn’t draw on your pension while you’re still working, even after the minimum pension age.
You haven’t chosen what to do with your leftover money, so the projection doesn’t save any of it (it’s treated as spent).

suggestions.title: Nothing left over each month
suggestions.text: You’re £483 a month short after spending, debts and regular savings. Look at your biggest spending categories, or reduce regular savings until it balances.

suggestions.title: Clear Credit card first
suggestions.text: It costs 24.9% a year, more than savings earn (3.5%), so paying extra off it is a guaranteed return. Personal loan (14.9%) and Car loan (9.9%) are next. Put a share of your leftover money into “Paying off debts faster” (most expensive first), or raise the monthly payment in Your figures.
howTo: Raise your monthly payment on Credit card from £90 to £140: at that rate it’s cleared by November 2028.
For a credit card, consider a 0% balance transfer: check the fee and how long the 0% lasts.
Set up a direct debit for the higher amount so it’s never late.

commitment.what: Pay £140 a month off Credit card, cleared by November 2028

suggestions.title: Build your emergency fund
suggestions.text: Your cash covers about 0.1 months of essential outgoings; your target is 3 (£6,750). A common aim is 3–6 months (£6,750–£13,500).

suggestions.title: Check for employer matching
suggestions.text: Your employer adds 3%. Many employers add more if you pay more — if yours does, that’s usually the best return available.

suggestions.title: Use your ISA allowance
suggestions.text: You have about £20,000 of this year’s £20,000 ISA allowance left. Growth and interest in an ISA are tax-free. For money you won’t need for at least five years, a stocks & shares ISA has historically beaten cash, but can fall in value.
howTo: Set up £1,660 a month into a stocks & shares ISA (or a cash ISA for money you’ll need within five years). Open one, or top up one you already have.
You have about £20,000 of this year’s allowance left, and 163 days until it resets on 5 April 2027.
Set the payment for payday so it happens without thinking about it.

commitment.what: Pay £1,660 a month into an ISA
